Let \(n=1985\), and let \(R=\underbrace{111\ldots 1}_{n\text{ ones}}\). Then

\[
a=8R,\qquad b=5R,
\]

so

\[
9ab=9\cdot 8R\cdot 5R=360R^2.
\]

Using

\[
R=\frac{10^n-1}{9},
\]

we get

\[
360R^2=40\left(R_{2n}-2R_n\right),
\]

where \(R_m=\underbrace{111\ldots 1}_{m\text{ ones}}\).

Now

\[
R_{2n}-2R_n=R_n\cdot 10^n-R_n
=\underbrace{11\ldots 110}_{n\text{ digits}}\underbrace{88\ldots 89}_{n\text{ digits}}.
\]

Thus

\[
360R^2=40\left(R_{2n}-2R_n\right)=10\cdot 4\left(R_{2n}-2R_n\right).
\]

Multiplying the pattern by \(4\) gives

\[
4\left(R_{2n}-2R_n\right)
=\underbrace{44\ldots 4}_{n-1\text{ fours}}3\underbrace{55\ldots 5}_{n-1\text{ fives}}6.
\]

Appending the final zero from the factor \(10\), the digit sum is

\[
4(n-1)+3+5(n-1)+6=9n.
\]

With \(n=1985\),

\[
9n=9\cdot 1985=17865.
\]

\[
\boxed{17865}
\]
